expectation: Membrane rings on myeloid cells (macrophages, monocytes, neutrophils): common, scattered single cells through the lamina propria/stroma between the crypts or glands, with more near the mucosal surface and in inflamed areas; the epithelium itself should be negative.
notes: No convincing CD11b-positive cell population. The signal is a haze over the tissue plus bright blobs that also sit on the bare glass, B to D show no membrane-ringed cells, and the CD66b partner channel has no structure of its own.
observed: A: yellow haze over the tissue, bright dots on the glass off the tissue as well as in it, streaks at the edges. B/C: diffuse haze over the stroma, a few irregular blobs, no rings. D: cloudy patches. E: the CD66b partner shows no cells, so row E tells us nothing.
why: The signal is haze that follows the tissue plus blobs that also appear off the tissue; no distinct population of ringed myeloid cells is visible at any scale.
